tinyCounterexample.interpretation: For a tiny object, the full serialization is already trivial. Streaming adds orchestration overhead, is much slower in this hosted sample, and does not provide a meaningful heap high-water advantage.

exactness.streaming: deterministic canonical character emission -> incremental FNV-1a

truthBoundary: This does not prove streaming fingerprinting is universally faster; it is slower in both measured scenarios.
RSS and V8 heap-capacity observations are process-shape specific and are not additive object-size accounting.
The streaming implementation is measured separately and has not yet replaced hashValue globally in this rung.
The tests preserve current serializer semantics; they are not an exhaustive ECMAScript/JSON conformance proof for arbitrary exotic values.
No datacenter, energy, cloud-cost, or fleet-density savings claim is established.
nextGate: Integrate streaming fingerprinting into the core hash path behind a deterministic threshold/policy so large canonical values can avoid whole-string high-water while tiny values can keep the cheaper monolithic path; replay the complete evidence ladder and measure the crossover.
